documents.title: EN 18286 + ISO/IEC 42001 management system
documents.summary: One management-system programme with two sets of criteria: EN 18286:2026 for AI Act QMS readiness and ISO/IEC 42001:2023 for certification-style assessment.

defaults.coverageRule: Unknown, not_run, inconclusive and error do not count as pass.
defaults.statement: Diagnostics support an audit assessment and do not constitute legal compliance or a conformity certificate.

reporting.limitations: Assurance conclusions do not constitute ISO/IEC 42001 certification by an accredited certification body, a conformity assessment under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, or legal advice.

controlObjectives.statement: Assess whether the AI risk assessment process is defined and is performed at planned intervals and after significant changes.

addresses.justification: Steps P01 and P02 test every requirement of clause 6.1.2 as listed in the licensed copy; the objective adds sampling of individual AI systems.
Steps P02 and P03 test performance of assessments at planned intervals and after significant change, which is all of clause 8.2.
EN 18286 planning also covers quality objectives and change planning that this objective does not test.

items.title: AI risk assessment: design and operation
items.objective: Assess whether the AI risk assessment process is defined and is performed at planned intervals and after significant changes.

procedures.text: Inspect the documented risk assessment process, its criteria and the approved risk acceptance levels.
Trace a sample of AI systems through risk identification, analysis, evaluation and treatment.
Verify that assessments were repeated at planned intervals and after significant changes.
Reconcile assessment results with the risk treatment plan and the impact assessment.

items.signOffGate: Independent reviewer clears blocking notes and approves the exact revision; lead approval where material.

procedures.text: Describe criterion, missing/conflicting evidence and efforts to obtain it.

documents.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 to the EU AI Act (amended)

useCase.intendedUsers: Lead auditors and reviewers on engagements that use either framework as criteria.
useCase.purpose: Show where ISO/IEC 42001 audit evidence also bears on AI Act obligations, and where it does not.
useCase.assumptions: Relationships compare what each requirement demands, not how an organisation implements it. No inference may be drawn from requirements that are not mapped.

entries.justification: Both require an established risk process. ISO/IEC 42001 targets risks to the organisation's AI objectives; Art. 9(1) requires a lifecycle risk-management system for one high-risk system. Neither contains the other.
Performing assessments at planned intervals supports the 'maintained' element of Art. 9(1) but does not establish the system-level risk-management system.

useCase.intendedUsers: Lead auditors and reviewers on engagements that use either framework as criteria.

useCase.assumptions: Relationships compare what each requirement demands, not how an organisation implements it. No inference may be drawn from requirements that are not mapped.

entries.justification: Annex ZA relates these clauses to Art. 17(1); Art. 17(2) to (4) are outside it, and the clauses also cover topics beyond Art. 17. At article level the two only overlap.

legalEffect.basis: EN 18286:2026 Annex ZA (Table ZA.1); reference published by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274.
legalEffect.conditions: Only for the Art. 17(1) rows and conditions of Table ZA.1, and only while the reference stays published in the Official Journal. A presumption follows from conformity with the standard; it is not an audit conclusion.
